name: Jharkhand '108' ambulance workers' strike
about: The Jharkhand Pradesh Ambulance Employees Union began protests on 6 October and held a one-day strike on 16 October. A strike planned for 21 October was put off after assurances from the health department; the union has now called an indefinite statewide strike from 26 October.
demands: Pay salaries pending since July; reinstate dismissed staff; stop salary deductions; EPF, ESI, overtime and gratuity; run the service at district level through the civil surgeon.

context.question: Why are Jharkhand's 108 ambulance workers striking?
context.short: 108 is India's toll-free emergency ambulance number. In Jharkhand, ambulance staff say their salaries have not been paid since July, and their union has called an indefinite statewide strike from 26 October.
explainer: More than 300 ambulances answer the 108 emergency number across Jharkhand.

The Jharkhand Pradesh Ambulance Employees Union began protests on 6 October and held a one-day strike on 16 October. A strike planned for 21 October was put off after assurances from the health department. With no result, the union has called an indefinite statewide strike from 26 October.
impact: If the strike goes ahead, more than 300 ambulances could stop running. As of 22 October, the health department had not announced alternative arrangements.
Workers want salaries pending since July paid, dismissed staff reinstated, deductions stopped, EPF, ESI, overtime and gratuity paid, and the service run at district level through the civil surgeon.
